meta.og_description: Learn how free, leader-facilitated eight-week Homeward Circles meet online or in the Fort Worth area to practice Christian meditation, explore Scripture honestly, and carry faith into everyday life.

hero.heading: A small community where faith becomes real.
hero.lead: A Homeward Circle is a leader-facilitated group of six to eight people who meet for eight weeks—to share life, become present to God, explore honest questions, and practice the rhythms of faith inspired by Jesus. It is not only a place to discuss spiritual ideas; it is a place to learn and practice the how-to of spiritual life together. At the end, you decide whether to continue. There is no ongoing commitment.
hero.logistics: In person in the Fort Worth area or online · No cost · Six to eight people · Eight weeks

heart.image_alt: Six adults of varied ages and backgrounds seated comfortably in a relaxed Homeward Circle conversation
heart.caption: A consistent group. A guided rhythm. Space to be honest and known.
heart.heading: Unhurried. Honest. Practiced together.
heart.lead: A Circle is not a class where one person has all the answers, and it is more than a weekly conversation about faith. It is a consistent group—the same people each week—learning to become present to God and one another through shared practice, Scripture, and honest dialogue.
heart.body: Leaders facilitate rather than lecture. We practice together, notice what is happening within us, explore Scripture and the teachings of Jesus with honesty, and carry a concrete rhythm into the week. No one is asked to pretend or reach the same conclusion.
heart.urgency_heading: Circles form as the right people connect.
heart.urgency_text: Tell us you are interested, and we will get to know you before helping you join a group.

rhythm.heading: A simple rhythm with room to breathe.
rhythm.intro: The flow shifts from week to week, but every gathering makes room for simple hospitality, a practice we experience together, honest dialogue, and a rhythm to carry into everyday life.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.description: Settle in, reconnect, and feel at home—no rush.

steps.title: Become present
steps.description: Practice breath prayer, Christian meditation, silence, or another guided rhythm together.

steps.title: Explore
steps.description: Engage a story, Scripture passage, or teaching inspired by Jesus with curiosity.

steps.title: Share
steps.description: Speak honestly about what is alive for you, explore the text together, or simply listen. No pressure.

steps.title: Carry it home
steps.description: Choose a simple practice that helps you notice God and live with greater presence during the week.

sample.heading: What one session might feel like.
sample.intro: This shows the tone and flow — not a rigid script. A gathering runs about 90 minutes. Week one is about getting to know each other and feeling welcome: everyone's invited to share, and anyone can pass. There's no pressure to perform.
sample.title: The Invitation Home
sample.description: An approachable first gathering about belonging, spiritual longing, and what it means to begin honestly.

items.title: Settling in and getting to know each other
items.body: We settle in over coffee, tea, and snacks — no rush — then begin with a simple question: What drew you here? Everyone's welcome to share, or to pass.

items.title: A guided breath prayer
items.body:
A simple practice that calms the body, steadies the mind, and helps us become present to the presence of God — with us and within us. As we breathe, we grow more grounded, open, and loving.
Breathing in: Here I am.
Breathing out: You are here.

items.title: A story and reflection
items.body: A short, familiar story Jesus told — the son who comes home to a father running to meet him — and an open, honest conversation about God, grace, and how each of us hears it.

items.title: Honest conversation
questions: When you hear the word home, what image or longing comes to mind?
Where do you most long to experience welcome or belonging?
What do you make of a love that runs to meet us before we've figured it all out?

items.title: A practice to carry home
items.body: A few minutes of breath prayer on a few days this week, using the same words: Here I am. You are here.

items.title: A simple blessing
items.body: We each offer a word for how we're leaving, and close with a blessing: May you know you are received before you have everything figured out — and may you notice the presence of God on the road ahead.

fit.heading: Circles are made for real people in real seasons.
fit.fit_heading: You may feel at home if...
fit_items: You still long for God, even if your faith has changed.
You want depth without rigid certainty.
You are willing to listen, practice, and be known.
You want a community inspired by the life and teachings of Jesus.
You believe transformation happens in relationship.
not_items: Commit before first getting to know us.
Commit beyond eight weeks — you choose whether to continue.

final.heading: Let us know a Circle interests you.
final.lead: Share your information, ask a question, or start a conversation when you are ready.

distinctives.heading: Practice the way. Explore honestly. Carry it into life.
distinctives.intro: Many groups are built mainly around discussing ideas. A Homeward Circle includes thoughtful conversation, but does not stop there. Every week, we practice, reflect, and take something concrete into daily life.

items.title: Practice the way.
items.description: Learn time-tested practices such as breath prayer, Christian meditation, silence, inspired reading, and daily reflection—and actually practice them together.

items.title: Explore honestly.
items.description: Engage Scripture and the life of Jesus with curiosity. Bring questions, doubt, lived experience, and different perspectives without pressure for a polished or predetermined answer.

items.title: Carry it into life.
items.description: Take home a simple rhythm and learn to notice God, wonder, and love in ordinary moments—so faith becomes more present, peaceful, joyful, and embodied.

practice_example.heading: Here I am. You are here.
practice_example.lead: In a Circle, we do not only explain breath prayer—we practice it together, reflect on what we notice, and carry it into the week.

steps.title: Settle
steps.description: Let your body become still and notice the natural rhythm of your breathing.

steps.title: Return
steps.description: When the mind wanders, gently return to the breath and the words.

steps.title: Carry it home
steps.description: Practice for three to five minutes on a few days this week.

practice_example.closing: The point is not to perform the practice perfectly. It is to become more available to God, yourself, and the life in front of you.
